stem: Rohan holds one hand under a warm tap and the other under a cool tap. Then he puts both hands into the same bucket of room water.

parts.text: Can he trust touch alone to say whether the room water is hot or cold?

options.text: No. The two hands disagree, so he should measure the temperature.
Yes. Touch still tells the true temperature of the room water.
Yes. The hand that was under the warm tap feels the true temperature.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: After different prior temperatures, the hands disagree, so touch is not enough.

teacher.key_rationale: Touch depends on what the hands felt before. When the hands disagree, temperature must be measured.
